primitives.name: Cache Staleness Threshold
primitives.verbatim_quote: Wiring `cacheControlHeader(cachePolicyFor(...))` + `revalidate` changes caching behavior (staleness window) — a product call.
primitives.assumptions: Caching policy is deterministic and time-bound; revalidation occurs at fixed intervals.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_revalidate < T_s, stale data may be served without refresh.

layer2.mapping: State transition function for cache invalidation under time-based triggers; modeled as a discrete event system with bounded delay.
layer2.telemetry: Observed cache hit ratio and stale data frequency

primitives.name: Merkle Root Integrity Bound
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Proof-of-record Merkle root truncates at 500 picks** — the integrity claim silently covers only the first 500.
primitives.assumptions: Merkle tree construction is deterministic and prefix-closed; integrity is bounded to n_max.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When n > n_max, I(n) becomes unreliable due to truncation.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a bounded hash commitment scheme where integrity is only guaranteed up to a fixed cardinality.
layer2.telemetry: Number of picks included in Merkle root vs. total picks

primitives.name: Secret Scan Guardrail
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **Secret-scan guardrail is a no-op in CI** — it scans the (empty) git stage, so CI's secret gate always passes on 0 files.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S': 'set of scanned files', 'G(S)': 'guardrail outcome, binary', 'S_{CI}': 'subset of staged files in CI'}
primitives.assumptions: Guardrail operates on file set S; in CI, S_{CI} = ∅ implies G(S_{CI}) = true.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When |S_{CI}| = 0, G(S_{CI}) is vacuously true, leading to false security.

layer2.mapping: A conditional state machine where guardrail outcome depends on input set size; modeled as a binary predicate over file sets.
layer2.telemetry: Number of files scanned in CI vs. number of secrets detected
